title: Catalog bench selection workflow and compatibility map - Crane Analytics

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-24 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Tom Rivers (CTO - Crane Analytics), Priya Sethi (Lead ML Eng), Diego Marquez (SRE), Aisha Khan (Product)

Auto Summary: Short demo of Catalog + Optimize. Walkthrough of selecting open models, running bench jobs, interpreting compatibility matrix and kernel mapping. Addressed questions about private deployment and audit logs.

[00:00:00] Lena: All right good morning everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45, 50 minutes, we'll try to run the catalog flow and then leave time for Q&A. Uh Marcus is gonna do the deep demo part.
[00:00:12] Tom: Great thanks Lena, we wanted to see how you would approach selecting open models for our customer support summarization workload. Quick context, we care about p95 under 300ms and cost per 1k tokens in a particular band.
[00:00:25] Marcus: Got it, thanks Tom. Quick clarifying q, are you mainly looking at hosted first or are you planning to run dedicated pools in the near term?
[00:00:34] Priya: We will try hosted to move fast but ultimately need private VPC for PCI data, so need to know which models and quant profiles map well to our on-prem infra.
[00:00:46] Diego: And infra notes: we have A100s today and exploring smaller T4-like nodes for edge cases. Also kubernetes 1.25 with onprem node pools.
[00:00:58] Marcus: Excellent, that helps. I'm going to share my screen - opening the Catalog in Console - you'll see filters on model size, family, quantization support, and a compatibility column which is the matrix we use to surface kernel mapping and runtime fit.
[00:01:12] [screen share noise/brief pause]
[00:01:20] Marcus: So first step is shortlisting by workload signature. I'm choosing small to medium conversational models, boosting for instruction-following. The catalog shows our curated open models and we also annotate the benchmark archetypes - throughput, p50/p95 latency, and token cost.
[00:01:38] Aisha: Real quick, how accurate are those latency numbers? Are they from our hosted fleet or synthetic runs?
[00:01:44] Marcus: Good question. They come from a mix: standardized bench runs on our hosted hardware with sequence length profiles, plus historical production traces when available. There's a confidence score. For your case with shorter summaries they trend lower but we always recommend running the bench with your prompt set.
[00:01:59] Priya: Speaking of prompts, do you have a template? We have several prompt permutations and a lot of system token prefixes.
[00:02:07] Lena: Yep, we'll share the bench template after this call; Marcus will include the script to run in your staging environment.
[00:02:14] [00:02:14] Marcus: Now I'm toggling the compatibility map - note the matrix rows are models, columns are runtime features: A100 FP16 kernels, int8 quantization, KV cache size estimates, and preferred batch sizes. For example this open model x-2-7b shows good int8 support and small KV footprint, so it maps well to T4-like nodes.
[00:02:35] Tom: Can you explain kernel mapping a bit? We don't want surprises where a model runs fine on one node and then suddenly falls off in production.
[00:02:42] Marcus: Sure. Kernel mapping is our internal heuristic + measured mapping from model op profile to optimized kernels. For certain attention variants we pick a different CUDA kernel or fallback to slower paths. The compatibility matrix also notes when a model is 'fragile' with a particular quant profile - e.g., some open models show quality regressions at int4. We annotate that.
[00:03:05] Priya: Do you measure quality regressions automatically or is that human curated?
[00:03:10] Marcus: It's hybrid. We run eval suites and also surface regression flags from our Optimize pipeline where we compare outputs on seed prompts. Sometimes names get a little off in the auto detection - it's not perfect - but it's a good early signal.
[00:03:23] Diego: On the routing side, if one model is cheaper but slightly slower, can you route low-criticality traffic to it?
[00:03:30] Marcus: Yes, we have smart routing rules. Policies can be latency-first, cost-first, or tier-based. You can specify SLOs per route and we automatically fallback to a compatible variant if the primary is degraded. There was a question earlier about prefix caching - we do KV cache and prefix cache which often reduces token generation latency, especially on repeated conversations.
[00:03:49] Aisha: How do you handle the VPC/private plane differences? If we pilot on hosted then move to private, will the compatibility data hold?
[00:03:58] Marcus: The compatibility matrix accounts for hardware differences. We run the bench on both hosted flavors and on private images in our private sandbox when we have customer on-prem runs. Guarantees are obviously better for dedicated/private because you control the fleet. But the catalog heuristics are meant to be portable: they indicate expected changes if you change from A100 to T4 or if you use int8 quantization.
[00:04:20] Tom: Any gotchas with KV cache and multi-tenant hosted?
[00:04:24] Marcus: On hosted we use tenant isolation for cache and we expose cache hits in metrics. Multi-tenant caches may have different hit rates, so we show expected delta ranges in the bench output.
[00:04:34] [00:04:34] Priya: Can we walk through an example? Say we start with model a-open-7b and model b-llamax-6.7 - how do we pick which to run in pilot?
[00:04:43] Marcus: I'll do side-by-side. Model a-open-7b: higher quality on summarization evals, p95 ~ 380ms on A100 FP16, int8 hasn't been fully validated but expected to drop cost by 35%. Model b-llamax-6.7: slightly cheaper baseline, p95 ~ 270ms, but lower ROUGE/chrF on our summarization set. So pick depending on whether you care about p95 or final summary quality; or route 80/20 to test both.
[00:05:11] Tom: Our requirement was p95 < 300ms ideally, and quality must not drop more than 3% on our eval set.
[00:05:18] Marcus: For that constraint I'd suggest model b for latency, but run a small A/B on a-open restricted to high-value users. We'll flag any quality delta via Optimize's regression alerts during the pilot.
[00:05:30] Aisha: Do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs? We have a parsing layer downstream.
[00:05:36] Marcus: Yes, Catalog entries include structured-output support flags. We also show whether the model is calibrated for tool-calling (some models are better at JSON output). That lives in the model metadata.
[00:05:47] [00:05:47] Priya: About cost estimates - how granular are they? Do you show per-token cost by runtime and quant?
[00:05:53] Marcus: We provide cost/call and per-token estimates for common runtimes and quant configs. The Optimize tab suggests quant profile and batching that minimize unit cost while meeting latency constraints. It's an optimization problem with knobs you can tune.
[00:06:06] Diego: If we want to run a bench ourselves on staging, what's the recommended cluster size?
[00:06:11] Marcus: For preliminary bench you can run on 2-4 A100s with batch sizes matching your production patterns. The bench template will include concurrency and sequence-length histograms. For true p95 we recommend longer runs with production-like arrival patterns.
[00:06:24] Tom: Security questions: SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs - do you expose model-level audit logs in private?
[00:06:32] Lena: Yes, for Private deployments we ship audit logs, KMS integration, and support SAML/SSO and RBAC. We'll attach our security pack in the follow-up.
[00:06:41] Priya: One more — when you talk about quant profiles and int4, how brittle is the quality? We've seen hallucinations increase with aggressive quant.
[00:06:50] Marcus: Right, int4 can be brittle. That's why Optimize ties quality monitoring to quantization proposals: if a regression is detected on your eval set we'll alert and automatically recommend a safer profile or A/B revert. The catalog flags models that historically degrade more than X% at a given quant level.
[00:07:08] [00:07:08] Aisha: Ops question: what telemetry do we get during pilot? Token-level cost, per-route latency, KV cache hit rates?
[00:07:15] Marcus: All of that. Console shows per-route token breakdown, p50/p95 latency by model/route, cost, and KV cache metrics. You can export to your analytics or push traces via open telemetry.
[00:07:26] Tom: Ok let's talk timeline. We want a pilot with sample traffic next week if possible.
[00:07:31] Lena: We can get you a shortlist and bench template today, Marcus can help run the first bench in staging. Diego if you can share access and sample prompts we'll aim for a bench by mid next week.
[00:07:42] Priya: Also please include example run outputs and the compatibility csv so we can import into our internal matrix.
[00:07:49] Marcus: Will do. The compatibility csv includes kernel hints and expected memory footprints. Note sometimes model names are slightly different in third-party repos, so double check mapping column - we've seen LAmaX vs LlamaX mismatches in some scrapes.
[00:08:03] [brief chuckle]
[00:08:08] Diego: Any commercial discussions now? Pricing for pilot vs production?
[00:08:12] Lena: We'll send pilot pricing (time-limited credits or trial reserved capacity) and then options for Dedicated or Private. Pricing sheet will be in the follow-up.
[00:08:21] Aisha: Can you remind us which team owns the bench templates once they're shared - we might want to adapt them.
[00:08:26] Marcus: We'll hand over the templates and you own them; we support tweaks and can run the bench as a managed service if you prefer.
[00:08:33] Tom: Great. Last question - is there a recommended way to handle fallback when a model mismatch occurs? E.g. if primary fails quality gating do you automatically switch?
[00:08:42] Marcus: You can configure automatic fallback to a pinned variant or to a higher-cost but more stable model. We also support canary traffic and automatic forced-revert if regression thresholds are exceeded.
[00:08:54] [00:08:54] Priya: Ok that's helpful. Thanks Marcus.
[00:08:58] Lena: Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Redwood sends bench template + compatibility csv + security pack. Crane provides prompt set and access. Plan pilot next week. We'll follow up in email with proposed times.
[00:09:12] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks all.

Questions (captured):
- How accurate are catalog latency estimates for private infra?
- How brittle are int4 quant profiles for our summarization workload?
- Can routing easily be set to meet p95 SLOs?

References mentioned: bench template (link), compatibility csv (link), security pack (link), perf spreadsheet (link)
